title: N+1 queries & eager loading (advanced)
summary: Why lazy relationship access in a loop explodes into N+1 queries — and the fixes.
body:
Why lazy relationship access in a loop explodes into N+1 queries — and the fixes.

Why it matters: ORMs make relationships look like attributes. Touching one in a loop silently runs one query per row; at 1 000 rows that is 1 001 round-trips.

SQL ↔ ORM: SQLAlchemy selectinload/joinedload. Prisma include/select. SQL: one JOIN or WHERE id = ANY(...).
why: ORMs make relationships look like attributes. Touching one in a loop silently runs one query per row; at 1 000 rows that is 1 001 round-trips.
objectives: Know when a JOIN duplicates parent rows.
pitfalls: Fixing N+1 with an index (it only makes each query faster).
mappingNotes: SQLAlchemy selectinload/joinedload. Prisma include/select. SQL: one JOIN or WHERE id = ANY(...).
teachAlong: Cause: Why lazy relationship access in a loop explodes into N+1 queries — and the fixes.
Effect: run the exercise and read the gate's rule ids.

example.sql: SELECT a.name, b.title FROM authors a JOIN books b ON b.author_id = a.id;

exercise.prompt: Answer every question — each wrong option explains why it is wrong.

questions.prompt: You load 50 authors, then access author.books in a loop. With lazy loading, how many queries run?

options.why: Only if the books were eager-loaded; lazy loading fetches each author's books on first access.

options.text: 51 — one for the authors plus one per author (the N+1 problem)

options.why: That is what selectinload / include gives you — not the lazy default.

questions.prompt: Which call loads authors AND their books in a fixed number of queries?

options.text: SQLAlchemy: select(Author).options(selectinload(Author.books)); Prisma: findMany({ include: { books: true } }); SQL: one JOIN

options.why: That is still one query per author.
An index makes each query faster but does not reduce the number of queries.

questions.prompt: When is joinedload (one JOIN) worse than selectinload (two queries)?

options.text: For one-to-many collections: the JOIN repeats every author column for each book row

options.why: Large collections multiply rows in a JOIN; selectinload avoids that duplication.
Row duplication happens on every database.
